questions.explanation:
## Why This Is Asked

Beginners learn scheduling with deadlines via DP by introducing a time dimension and reconstruction, mirroring knapsack intuition but with feasibility via deadlines.

## Key Concepts

- 0/1 knapsack style DP with time as capacity
- Sorting by deadlines to ensure feasibility
- Backtracking to recover chosen jobs and their intervals

## Code Example

```javascript
function schedule(p, d, w){
  const n = p.length;
  const idx = Array.from({length: n}, (_,i) => i).sort((a,b)=> d[a]-d[b]);
  // would build dp[n+1][T], T = max(d)
}
```

## Follow-up Questions

- How would preemption change the DP?
- How to optimize space to O(T) with backtracking?

## Why This Is Asked

Tests DP with orientation state, exact turn constraints, and path reconstruction under a grid, a common Google/Databricks style problem.

## Key Concepts

- DP with 4D state (i,j,t,dir)
- Transition increments t when dir changes
- Backpointer for path reconstruction
- Edge-case: unreachable states when K exceeds max turns

## Code Example

```javascript
// Pseudo-state transitions sketch
dp[i][j][t][d] = max(
  dp[i][j-1][t - (d!=0 ? 1:0)][0],
  dp[i-1][j][t - (d!=1 ? 1:0)][1]
) + grid[i][j]
```

## Follow-up Questions

- How would you reduce memory to O(n*m) and still reconstruct the path?
- How to handle K larger than possible turns or grids with zero weights?
